It's a big shout for a player that's only just broken into the England team, but her 60-minute debut against Greece couldn't have gone much better. "It was really special," the Chelsea midfielder told ITV Sport after the game. "I am very happy and proud. It was a bit of a rush before the game and I lost my phone! messages.text: Martinez calls out Man Utd hierarchy

metadata.summary: Manchester United's Lisandro Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club’s hierarchy after their 2-0 Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid.
metadata.content: Man Utd defender Lisandro Martinez extraordinarily calls out club's hierarchy after Atletico Madrid loss in Champions League | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man Utd defender Lisandro Martinez extraordinarily calls out club's hierarchy after Atletico Madrid loss in Champions League Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez astonishingly attacks club's hierarchy after Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid; Martinez told Amazon Prime : "We expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete"; he added: "I expect more from our technical director" Wednesday 14 October 2026 00:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Man Utd boss Michael Carrick is asked about Lisandro Martinez's comments after the loss at Atletico Madrid Manchester United's Lisandro Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club’s hierarchy after their 2-0 Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid. In an astonishing post-match interview, the Argentina international criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad. The defender said he had expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox, in the most recent transfer window in which they failed to improve their options at left-back and up front. Man Utd spent £155m on just four major summer signings after a third-place Premier League finish last season, which earned a return to the Champions League for the first time in three years. messages.text: 'State of the Game' report finds most English clubs living on financial brink

metadata.summary: The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has produced a 'State of the Game' report, which has taken a forensic look at English football over the past 18 months, concluding that the game's finances are dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster.
metadata.content: 'State of the Game': Independent Football Regulator's report finds most English clubs living on financial brink | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content 'State of the Game': Independent Football Regulator's report finds most English clubs living on financial brink The Independent Football Regulator published its draft ‘State of the Game’ report on Tuesday, which found that while English football generated £9bn in revenue last season, 94 per cent of clubs in the top five divisions were loss-making Geraint Hughes Sports News Correspondent Tuesday 13 October 2026 17:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News reporter Geraint Hughes explains the Independent Football Regulator's 'State of the Game' report, which explores how most English clubs are living on the brink of financial ruin The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has produced a 'State of the Game' report, which has taken a forensic look at English football over the past 18 months, concluding that the game's finances are dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster. The IFR added that interest and investment from around the world continues to grow within English football, but the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform. metadata.summary: Alexander Zverev celebrated becoming the year-end No 1 with a 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-1) victory over Alexander Bublik to reach the quarter-finals at the Shanghai Masters.
metadata.content: Shanghai Masters: Alexander Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with win over Alexander Bublik as Katie Boulter bows out of Wuhan Open | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Shanghai Masters: Alexander Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with win over Alexander Bublik as Katie Boulter bows out of Wuhan Open Alexander Zverev struggles with ankle issues but does enough to reach his 40th Masters 1000 quarter-final of his career in China; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports Tuesday 13 October 2026 15:04, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexander Bublik and Alexander Zverev starred in the point of the week at the Shanghai Open! Alexander Zverev celebrated becoming the year-end No 1 with a 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-1) victory over Alexander Bublik to reach the quarter-finals at the Shanghai Masters. Zverev, who won the French Open and US Open this year, never looked 100 per cent comfortable, and admitted his "ankle was acting up" following his win. The top seed will take on ninth seed Alex de Minaur next after the Australian produced one of his best performances of the year to beat Karen Khachanov in straight sets 6-3 6-4 to advance.
